correctness.rationale: Gaussianity makes coherence exp[−sigma²tau² Q/2] with Q the nonnegative kernel double integral of the three-sign modulation. Partitioning the integral gives Q=2L−10+4(e^(−a)+e^(−c))+8e^(−b)−4(e^(−a−b)+e^(−b−c))+2e^(−L), corroborated by an independent interval-state integral recursion for 1000 test triples. For fixed middle length b and a+c=L−b, dQ/da=4(1−e^(−b))(e^(−c)−e^(−a)), negative for a<c and positive for a>c; uniquely minimizes at a=c. Along this locus dQ/db=4e^(−a)(1+e^(−b))−8e^(−b); its sign equals sign[2b+2log cosh(b/2)−L]. This continuous strictly increasing scalar from −L to positive at b=L has a unique interior root; both boundary schedules lose. Bounds 0<log cosh(b/2)<b/2 force 1/4<a/L<1/3. Strict convexity of log cosh ensures monotonic ratio as L varies. Small-L root b=L/2−L²/32+O(L³) and gain Q_CPMG−Q_opt=L^4/256+O(L^5) are consistent; independent mpmath high-precision small-L expansion and thousands of unrestricted numerical competitors corroborate. The proof, not the sample search, establishes the universal unique minimum.

value.rationale: Exactly two-pulse timing is a natural constrained control optimization for Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dephasing. The theorem solves a continuous two-variable global problem in closed implicit form, proves uniqueness and sharp geometry, and separates the true finite-correlation coherence optimum from the commonly imposed zero-static-area Carr–Purcell schedule. A model-specific optimal control law is useful without asserting a new general control theorem or experimental superiority.

final_claim: For stationary centered Gaussian exponential-covariance pure-dephasing noise, exactly two unconstrained ideal sign-inverting pulses over L=T/tau have a unique global coherence-maximizing timing a=c=(L−b)/2, with b>0 the unique root L=2b+2log cosh(b/2). The first pulse fraction increases strictly from 1/4 toward 1/3, making symmetric quarter–three-quarter timing strictly suboptimal for all finite L>0.
limitations: Stationary centered Gaussian (not generic telegraph) exponential covariance, exactly two ideal instantaneous pulses.
No optimization over pulse count, finite pulse widths, correlation-parameter uncertainty or experimental hardware cost.
